title: Why a Good Company Can Still Be a Bad Investment
excerpt: A great business and a great stock price are not always the same thing. The missing piece is valuation.
content: A company can have strong sales, loyal customers and excellent management, yet its shares can still be too expensive. Investing is not only about asking whether a business is good. It is also about asking what you are paying for that business. Think of it like buying a ₹100 product for ₹300. The product may be excellent, but the price changes the deal. The same idea applies to stocks: business quality matters, but valuation matters too.

title: The ₹10 Test: Would Your Customer Miss You?
excerpt: A simple way to understand brand value: imagine your customer has only ₹10 and one choice to make.
content: Marketing is often treated as advertising, but strong marketing starts earlier. If your customer had only ₹10 to spend, would they remember your brand when choosing? That is the difference between attention and preference. A memorable product solves a clear problem, communicates simply and gives people a reason to return. Ads can create awareness, but the experience creates the brand.

title: Revenue Is Not the Same as Cash
excerpt: A business can report impressive revenue and still struggle to pay its bills. Here is why.
content: Revenue tells us how much a business has earned from sales under its accounting rules. Cash tells us how much money has actually moved into the business. If a company sells ₹10 lakh of products on credit, it may record revenue even though customers have not paid yet. This is why investors look beyond the sales number and study cash flow, receivables and working capital too.
